clue.text: Mainly leading role around Thursday

indicators.note: around says the word for leading wraps itself round the abbreviation for Thursday

parts.note: leading, as in the first or chief, is foremost
an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: An actor's main role is built around a Thursday performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading role' reads as one stage phrase, but the two words do separate jobs, and 'around' works on the first of them alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiomatic synonym for mostly or chiefly, in the greater number of cases.

clue.text: Flip gospeller almost into the sea by public hotel

indicators.note: into says the shortened gospel writer goes inside the poetic word for the sea

parts.note: foam is a poetic word for the sea

indicators.note: almost says the gospeller's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Matthew is one of the four gospel writers
something made public is out in the open
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An evangelist somersaults into the sea beside a pub or hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flip' looks like a verb of tumbling; it is the definition, in the sense of losing one's temper. 'Almost' cuts MATTHEW to MATTHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is informal for losing one's temper completely, and this idiom describes raging with froth on the lips.

clue.text: Copy page in souvenir article

indicators.note: in says the page abbreviation sits inside the word for souvenir

parts.note: a relic is a keepsake or souvenir of the past
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A copied page tucked inside a souvenir magazine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproduction or duplicate of an original object is an exact copy of it.

clue.text: Strike central heating snag

parts.note: to strike is to hit
CH is the estate agents' abbreviation for central heating

explanation.surface: A strike by heating engineers causes a problem with the central heating.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is a minor difficulty or obstacle, the same thing as a small problem holding things up.

clue.text: Mike leads playful disruption

parts.note: M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
someone who leads is chief, i.e. is the boss: IS CHIEF

explanation.surface: A boy called Mike is the ringleader in some lighthearted trouble-making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' is read as the verb phrase 'is chief', giving IS CHIEF after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmless naughtiness and pranks that cause annoyance are a fair description of the playful disruption.

clue.text: Keen husband dipped into small brook

indicators.note: dipped into says the husband abbreviation is plunged inside the small stream

parts.note: a rill is a small brook or stream

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic husband went paddling in a little stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keen' reads as eager, but here it is the adjective for a piercing, high sound, as a keen wind or a keening wail.
explanation.definitionFit: A keen sound is sharp and piercing, which is how a high-pitched, penetrating voice is described.

clue.text: Capital that is accepted by both sides in promoting Chinese principle

indicators.note: accepted by says the archaic word for that is taken in between the two outer letters
both sides in picks the first and last letters of the word promoting

parts.note: yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yonder
yang is the active, masculine principle in Chinese philosophy, paired with yin

explanation.surface: A capital whose ideas are accepted on both sides while promoting a Chinese philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the capital city of North Korea, the seat of its government.

clue.text: Scramble to get on with artist above suspicion

indicators.note: in a down clue, above puts the artist abbreviation on top of the next piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
a suspicion of something, such as garlic, is a trace of it

explanation.surface: A scramble to get on with an artist who is above suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspicion' means a slight hint here, not mistrust.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the fierce competitive struggle for advancement at work, a scramble to get ahead.

clue.text: Duty of the superior toff, being above inferior English press

indicators.note: in a down clue, being above stacks the word for toff over the rest

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a posh upper-class person
less can mean lower in rank or inferior
to press someone is to compel or force them to act

explanation.surface: A toff looks down on the lowly English press.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase is the idea that privilege brings responsibility: the obligation of the well-born to act generously.

clue.text: Praise cast for acquiring favourite snack

indicators.note: acquiring says the shuffled letters take in the word for favourite
cast in the sense of thrown into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Praise was showered on someone for getting a favourite snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' is not a theatre company but the anagram signal, giving APISER; 'acquiring' then takes in the pet.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bite of food or drink taken before a meal to whet the hunger counts as a snack.

clue.text: Best expose cheat

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them publicly
to do someone is slang for to cheat or swindle them

explanation.surface: It is best to expose a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to beat or surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To best an opponent is to beat or surpass them, the same as going one better.

clue.text: American sectarians hard on English novelist

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the hard abbreviation after the novelist

parts.note: Kingsley and Martin Amis are English novelists
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: American religious groups come down hard on an English writer.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a strict Anabaptist community in Pennsylvania and elsewhere, a sect living apart from modern life.

clue.text: "Great goal" is all you'll hear a girl raving

indicators.note: you'll hear says the word for all is taken by its sound

parts.note: wholly means entirely, all

indicators.note: raving, as in wild or mad, signals the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl raves that a great goal is everything she wants to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred cup of Arthurian legend has become an idiom for any ultimate, much-sought aim or prize.

clue.text: Theft regularly involving farm tool yonks ago

indicators.note: involving says the alternate letters wrap round the word for farm
regularly picks the first, third and fifth letters of Theft

parts.note: a ranch is a large farm, especially for cattle

explanation.surface: A farm tool was stolen long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yonks ago' is British slang for a very long time ago, fair for a prehistoric object.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an archaeological term for a Stone Age flint axe-like cutting implement, a tool from ages past.

clue.text: Wrapping a card, crease fancy cloth

indicators.note: Wrapping says the jumbled letters enclose the card word
fancy as a verb of imagining, so the letters are reinvented in a new order

parts.note: a SIM card goes in a mobile phone

explanation.surface: Someone wraps a card in fancy fabric and puts a crease in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective for the cloth, but it signals the anagram, giving CASERE; the phone card sits within it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a plain-woven woollen fabric, a variant of kerseymere, used for suits.

clue.text: Killer's headless chickens?

indicators.note: headless says the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a slayer is a killer, so Killer's gives slayer's

explanation.surface: A killer goes round beheading chickens.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: hens are prized for laying eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hens kept for their eggs are called by the egg-producing role, so chickens are an example.

clue.text: Certainly true, cunningly hiding medals

indicators.note: hiding says the jumbled letters conceal the medals inside them
cunningly, as in craftily, says the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OBEs are medals, awards in the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: It is certainly true that someone has cunningly hidden their medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'True' sits beside 'Certainly' as if part of the definition, but it is the anagram fodder; 'cunningly' makes TURE.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a stock Irish expression of assent meaning of course or undoubtedly.

clue.text: US city making contribution to help a soldier

indicators.note: making contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A US city contributes to helping a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a city in western Texas on the Rio Grande, on the Mexican border.

clue.text: Voyeur embracing this setter over cardinal

indicators.note: embracing says the word for voyeur holds the setter inside it

parts.note: a prier is someone who pries or snoops, a voyeur

indicators.note: in a down clue, over says the setter's word is turned upwards, read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A peeping tom holds the setter over a cardinal of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman; it is the adjective meaning principal or chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means of first importance, chief, the same as foremost in rank.

clue.text: Cheat finally producing nothing for drug supplier?

parts.note: to fox is to trick or deceive

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of producing

parts.note: love means nothing, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: A cheat eventually produces nothing for a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drug supplier' hints at a dealer; the plant is the source of digitalis, a heart drug.
explanation.definitionFit: This plant provides digitalis, a medicine for heart conditions, so it literally supplies a drug.

clue.text: In which paperwork is sorted by folders

definitions.text: In which paperwork is sorted by folders

parts.words: In which paperwork is sorted by folders
parts.note: the clue reads as office filing, but describes the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes

explanation.surface: An office where documents are filed in folders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paperwork' is literal work with paper, and 'folders' are people who fold it.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Japanese craft, paper is shaped by people folding it, so folders sort paper work.

clue.text: Legendary figure, very large one, in hospital

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, very large

indicators.note: in says the one goes inside the hospital word

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a hospital
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A huge legendary figure lies in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the legendary Gaelic bard whose poems James Macpherson claimed to translate in the 1760s.

clue.text: Note glut concerning children

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a row over money
issue means offspring, children

explanation.surface: A musical note is glutted with concern for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a banknote: the definition is excessive printing of currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Printing and releasing too many banknotes or shares creates a glut of notes.

clue.text: Mount collage, initially with border

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of collage

parts.note: a limb is the edge or border of something, such as the sun's disc

explanation.surface: Mount a collage, starting with its border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' reads as framing a picture; it is the verb to go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a hill or stairs is to ascend or go up it.

clue.text: Perhaps lag behind on jeep, arriving at bend

parts.note: a lag is an old convict, an example of a crim, criminal

indicators.note: behind on picks the rear, last letter of jeep

explanation.surface: A slowcoach falls behind on a jeep ride and reaches a bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lag behind' looks like one phrase; 'lag' is the old convict, slang chiefly British.
explanation.definitionFit: To press something into small folds or waves, as with hair or pastry edges, is to bend it.

clue.text: Fool European singer

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish European singer.
explanation.definitionFit: This small moorland finch is a songbird, and birds are often singers in crosswords.

clue.text: Opera's wordplay about girl in islands

definitions.note: Opera's is read as opera is

indicators.note: in says the built piece sits between the two island letters

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island, twice for islands

indicators.note: about says the wordplay word goes round the girl's name

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An opera's punning lyrics about a girl living on islands.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Bellini's final opera, from 1835, set during the English Civil War.

clue.text: Peers interfere improperly in economic system

indicators.note: improperly, as in wrongly put together, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords improperly meddle in the economy.
explanation.definitionFit: A market economy where private businesses compete with little state control is this kind of economic system.
